issue.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/encode/starlette/discussions/1253
Originally posted by **flashgorman-chorus** July 26, 2021 I have installed `GZipMiddleware` with a `minimize_size` set to 1024. When I make a request that returns a response smaller than 1024, I expect the response will not be compressed and the `Content-Encoding` header will not be set to `gzip`. My testing, however, shows that the responses are always compressed and `Content-Encoding` is always set to `gzip`. Debugging the code, I see `send_with_gzip` is called but `message["more_body"]` is set to `True` the first time through, no matter what, from `testclient.py`: ```python async def stream_response(self, send: Send) -> None: await send( { "type": "http.response.start", "status": self.status_code, "headers": self.raw_headers, } ) async for chunk in self.body_iterator: if not isinstance(chunk, bytes): chunk = chunk.encode(self.charset) await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": chunk, "more_body": True}) await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": b"", "more_body": False}) ``` As a result, the key block of code in `gzip.py` that I expected to enter is skipped: ```python if len(body) < self.minimum_size and not more_body: # Don't apply GZip to small outgoing responses. await self.send(self.initial_message) await self.send(message) ``` Since `more_body` is `True`, it never enters this block. Perhaps this is just an aberration of the test client? Or I am doing something wrong?
issue.title: GZipMiddleware appears to not honor minimize_size
